subtype: Approach: adjusting after the first month in the new city [Revision]
passage: Sit down, and I'll tell you about my first flat in Bengaluru, because I got it wrong. I am Sachin. I had signed a lease in a lovely colony after one visit on a Sunday, when the roads were empty. On the first Monday, the drive to the office took an hour and a half. Six weeks in, I was so tired that I was snapping at my wife Uma over nothing. One night I finally said to myself: I chose with half the facts. There was a penalty for leaving the lease. I paid it anyway and moved to a flat ten minutes from the office. Uma called it the best money we ever wasted. My first choice was not stupid, beta. It was made with what I knew then.

subtype: Approach: adjusting after the first month in the new city [Revision]
passage:
Chetan had signed a lease in Thane before the monsoon, when the drive to his new office in Andheri looked fine on a map.
By July, it wasn't fine. Flooded roads turned the commute into two and a half hours each way. He left at seven and got home at ten. He fell asleep on the sofa most nights in his office clothes.
His colleague Divyansh finally said, "You look like a ghost. Why not move closer?"
"The lease has a three-month penalty."
"And how much are you losing in sleep?"
That weekend Chetan did the sums and thought it through. He'd picked Thane from photos and a Sunday visit, not from a single weekday commute in the rain. It wasn't a stupid choice, just one made with too little information.
He paid the penalty and moved to a smaller flat in Andheri East, twelve minutes from work. The first night he slept eight hours straight.

qa.q: How long was Chetan's commute each way in the flooded season?
qa.a: Two and a half hours each way.

qa.q: How did Chetan feel after the first night in the new flat?
qa.a: Chetan felt rested and relieved, sleeping eight hours straight after weeks of exhaustion.

qa.q: What else could Chetan do before signing his next lease?
qa.a: He could try the commute on a weekday at peak hour, in bad weather if possible, and ask colleagues about the area.

qa.q: How might Divyansh see Chetan's decision to move?
qa.a: Divyansh likely feels relieved and glad, having worried that Chetan looked like a ghost.

grounding: It shows someone finding the commute exhausting in the first months, moving closer despite a lease penalty and recognising the first choice was made with limited information.

subtype: Approach: adjusting after the first month in the new city [Revision]
passage:
In his first month in Chennai, Francis learned that a flat can look perfect on a Sunday and be a trap on a Monday.
He'd chosen a place in Tambaram because the rent was lower and the building had a gym. Then work began. The suburban train was packed, the bus from the station crawled, and he reached the office in Nungambakkam every morning drenched in sweat, an hour and a half after leaving home.
At the end of the month his colleague Pema asked, "Why do you look so tired every day?"
Francis thought about it on the train that evening. He'd chosen with the information he had then, which was very little. Now he knew better.
He talked to his landlord, paid the one-month penalty for leaving early, and found a room in T. Nagar. Twenty minutes to work.
The gym, he realised later, he'd used exactly twice.

qa.q: How many times did Francis use the gym?
How did Francis feel in his first month in Chennai, and what showed it?
qa.a: Francis was exhausted; he reached the office drenched in sweat, and Pema noticed how tired he looked every day.

qa.q: What else could Francis have done before choosing the first flat?
qa.a: He could have tried the commute on a working day at peak time and weighed it against the lower rent and the gym.

qa.q: How might Pema see the change after Francis moves?
qa.a: Pema would likely notice Francis looking less tired and feel glad the question prompted a change.

grounding: It shows someone finding the commute exhausting after the first month, moving closer despite a penalty and recognising the first choice was made with limited information.
